title: Coherent rigidified multiplicative lines on commutative group schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ a commutative group object in schemes over $S$, with multiplication $m$, identity $e$, and inverse satisfying the group diagrams [def-sc-group-scheme]. A coherent rigidified multiplicative line on $G$ consists of an invertible module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], a frame $u:\mathcal O_S\simeq e^*L$, and an isomorphism $\mu:p_1^*L\otimes p_2^*L\simeq m^*L$, using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] and sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Require associativity on $G^3$, symmetry under interchange, and both unit identities on the identity axes. Equivalently, for every $S$-scheme $U$, the framed points $(x,v)$ with $x:U\to G$ and $v:\mathcal O_U\simeq x^*L$ have associative commutative multiplication induced by $\mu$ and identity induced by $u$. Pull frames by the canonical tensor-pullback unit and composition comparisons, as in [def-sfb-split-torus-frame-model], and multiply them using the canonical tensor comparison [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison]. For any $b:T\to S$, let $G_T$ be the canonical base-changed group. An identification of a coherent line $A$ on $G_T$ with the restriction of a coherent line $E$ on $G$ is a module isomorphism $\operatorname{pr}_G^*E\simeq A$ preserving the identity frame and multiplication; equivalently its maps on all framed test points preserve identity and products.
